data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -N 1
#   -n 1
#   --mem=16G
#   -o log/process_join_annotate_counts.out
#   -e log/process_join_annotate_counts.err
#   --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p log

# Approximate Slurm stdout/stderr paths
exec >log/process_join_annotate_counts.out 2>log/process_join_annotate_counts.err

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=16G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm email notifications (--mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive job emails.

eval $(spack load --sh miniconda3)
source activate active-learning
python3 src/process_and_join_counts.py
python3 src/annotate_data.py
'
"
}
